Context/Background: Perianal fistulizing Crohn’s disease (CD) is a severe gastrointestinal disorder causing extensive mucosal damage with limited treatment options. Severe manifestations of the disease appear at higher rates in non-Europeans but the genetic and cellular mechanisms driving the disease phenotypes remain poorly understood. Herein, we tested whether pathologic determinants in the epithelial stem cell compartment could be detected at the transcript level in rectal organoids derived from a diverse patient population. Rectal organoid and mucosal cells from endoscopic biopsies of each patient having perianal fistulizing CD or no disease controls were prepared for and sequenced at the single cell level. After cell type annotations based on expressed marker genes, samples were analyzed by principal components, for differential transcript expression, cell type proportions, and pathway enrichment.
Prompt: Pathway analysis of transcriptional data from the mucosal epithelial (undifferentiated) cells of different CD phenotypes was performed against the Reactome database.  CD phenotypes compared are PIF (Perianal CD inflamed) vs PNI (Perianal CD non inflamed), PIF vs Control (non IBD), and PIN vs Control.  Please give a summary of the pathway enrichment results.  Focus on comparisons involving the PIF (inflamed) group.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
Differential Reactome pathway analysis was performed on undifferentiated mucosal epithelial cells comparing Perianal CD inflamed (PIF) vs non-inflamed Perianal CD (PNI) and PIF vs non-IBD controls. The provided Supplemental Table 2 lists significant pathways with GeneCount/direction, NES-like scores (negative values indicate downregulated), and “Direction” (“DOWN” for all PIF comparisons). Sample sizes, sequencing platform, and exact replicates are not specified.  

Keywords  
• RNA metabolism  
• Translation  
• Mitochondrial respiration  
• Cell cycle  
• Stress responses  

Candidate Genes  
FAU, LSM7, SNRPD1, PSMA7, COX4I1, NDUFB2, CDK4, PCNA  

Summary of PIF-associated pathway changes  
1. PIF vs Control (PIFvsCtrl):  
   –  METABOLISM OF RNA (GeneCount 105; score –105; DOWN)  
   –  TRANSLATION (77; –77; DOWN)  
   –  THE CITRIC ACID (TCA) CYCLE AND RESPIRATORY ELECTRON TRANSPORT (74; –74; DOWN)  
   –  CELLULAR RESPONSES TO STIMULI (73; –73; DOWN)  
   –  CELLULAR RESPONSES TO STRESS (71; –71; DOWN)  
   –  CELL CYCLE (63; –63; DOWN)  
   –  MITOCHONDRIAL TRANSLATION (55; –55; DOWN)  
   –  NEUTROPHIL DEGRANULATION (46; –46; DOWN)  
   –  TRANSCRIPTIONAL REGULATION BY TP53 (45; –45; DOWN)  

2. PIF vs PNI (PIFvsPNI):  
   –  METABOLISM OF RNA (76; –76; DOWN)  
   –  TRANSLATION (67; –67; DOWN)  
   –  THE CITRIC ACID (TCA) CYCLE AND RESPIRATORY ELECTRON TRANSPORT (61; –61; DOWN)  
   –  CELL CYCLE (55; –55; DOWN)  
   –  MITOCHONDRIAL TRANSLATION / INITIATION / ELONGATION / TERMINATION (47–48; DOWN)  
   –  CELLULAR RESPONSES TO STRESS (53; –53; DOWN)  
   –  TRANSCRIPTIONAL REGULATION BY TP53 (37; –37; DOWN)  
   –  CELLULAR RESPONSE TO CHEMICAL STRESS (36; –36; DOWN)  

Interpretation  
Across both PIF comparisons, core processes—RNA processing, ribosomal translation, mitochondrial respiration (TCA cycle, electron transport, mitochondrial translation), cell-cycle progression, and stress-response pathways—are markedly downregulated. This suggests that inflamed perianal CD epithelial stem cells exhibit a hypometabolic, hypo-proliferative state with impaired capacity for RNA maturation and protein synthesis, alongside reduced mitochondrial function. Concordant suppression of TP53-mediated responses and neutrophil-associated pathways further indicates altered damage‐response and immune-interaction programs in PIF.  

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Validate whether these transcript-level downregulations correlate with functional deficits (e.g., reduced OCR in mitochondrial assays).  
2. Examine single‐cell subtype contributions: are specific epithelial subsets driving the observed pathway suppression?  
3. Investigate upstream regulators (e.g., mTOR signaling, p53 activation) for potential therapeutic targeting to restore homeostatic transcription/translation.  
4. Assess whether similar pathway downregulation is observed in organoid models from non-European vs European ancestry to explore population-specific mechanisms.
